headline: GTA 6 pre-orders spark a big TTWO jump, Alphabet keeps climbing on cloud strength, but PLS.AX takes a nasty 4.7% hit today — here's what you need to know.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS got smacked today, dropping 4.7% to $5.88. Lithium prices remain under pressure and there's ongoing debate about whether Pilbara's Pilgangoora expansion will pay off in the current weak pricing environment. No specific news catalyst, but sentiment around ASX lithium stocks remains soft as the market waits for a genuine price recovery in China.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two had a cracking session last night, up nearly 5% to $239.28. The catalyst is straightforward: Rockstar Games confirmed GTA 6 pre-orders open on June 25 and dropped official cover art. Investors are betting this is one of the biggest game launches in history, and the excitement is real.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google's parent Alphabet gained 1.48% last night to $367.46, continuing its strong run. Recent earnings beat expectations by 94% and the company doubled its cloud backlog to $460 billion — that's a massive pipeline of future revenue. The market is rewarding that momentum.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE slipped 0.74% today to $94.44, essentially flat on the overall portfolio (down just $0.21 in total). Emerging market ETFs drifted slightly as the Aussie dollar held steady and there were no major catalysts from key markets like China today.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG eased 0.56% today to $76.83. This is a broad, diversified fund so it tends to follow the overall ASX tone — the local market had a mild down day with no strong bullish catalyst to push it higher.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: FUEL dipped 0.61% today to $8.10. Oil prices are soft — a recent ceasefire agreement has taken some geopolitical risk premium out of crude prices, which weighs on energy companies globally. The Iran situation has also complicated the demand/supply picture for 2026.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: GXAI nudged up 0.22% today to $18.16, a quiet but positive session. AI-related stocks globally are holding up well, supported by continued enthusiasm around the sector. No single catalyst today — just steady momentum.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft barely moved last night, up just 0.13% to $379.40. No major news out for MSFT specifically — it's treading water while the market watches Alphabet's cloud story steal some of the AI limelight. The stock is still down 14.4% from your cost base, so patience is required here.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS crept up 0.07% today to $525.46, essentially flat. It broadly tracks the US market, and with the S&P 500 and NASDAQ both having a solid night last night, this ETF is in good shape — up 1.89% on your total investment.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Lithium pain deepens — hold for now
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals dropped 4.7% today to $5.88, and you're now down 12.76% on your investment ($19.14 in the red). There's no single news event today but lithium prices remain weak and the Pilgangoora expansion debate is back in focus. Unless you have a conviction on a lithium price recovery in China this year, this is a hold-and-monitor situation — selling now would lock in the loss right before any potential bounce.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA 6 pre-orders open June 25 — momentum is real
watch_today.detail: Take-Two jumped 4.93% last night and you're now up 4.33% on your position ($24.71 profit). Rockstar confirmed GTA 6 pre-orders start June 25 with official cover art out. This is shaping up to be a monster launch. You'd be selling right before the biggest gaming event in years — hold and let this play out through the launch window.

watch_today.title: GOOG: Cloud backlog of $460B is a serious tailwind — hold strong
watch_today.detail: Alphabet is up 1.48% last night and you're sitting on a 19.52% gain ($19.49 profit) despite a small position. The story here is Alphabet's cloud business doubling its order backlog to $460 billion and beating recent earnings by 94%. The fundamentals are genuinely strong. No need to sell — this is a hold with upside.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Still underwater — watch for a catalyst
watch_today.detail: Microsoft is down 14.38% from your cost base (a $57.41 loss in AUD) and barely moved last night (+0.13%). There's no fresh news driving it. Alphabet is currently the stronger AI/cloud narrative in the market. MSFT isn't broken, but it needs a catalyst — watch for any product announcements or earnings updates before adding more.

watch_today.title: RBA holds rates — good news for Aussie assets generally
watch_today.detail: The RBA left interest rates on hold today, which is a relief for mortgage holders and generally positive for growth assets like your ETFs. It reduces pressure on Australian consumers and tends to support share prices. No action needed, but this is a tailwind for VDHG and the broader ASX.

watch_today.title: GTA 6 pre-orders June 25 — mark your calendar
watch_today.detail: Rockstar Games opens GTA 6 pre-orders next Wednesday, June 25. Expect significant media coverage and likely another pop in TTWO share price around that date. Worth keeping an eye on the price action next week — if it runs hard into the pre-order date, that could be a point to reassess your position.

markets.summary: Last night on Wall Street it was a strong session — the NASDAQ jumped 1.91% and the S&P 500 climbed 1.08%, both powered by tech stocks. Alphabet and Take-Two were clear standouts in your portfolio. Gold slipped 1.38% to around $4,166 USD/oz, possibly as investors felt comfortable taking on more risk and moving out of 'safe haven' assets. Oil was essentially flat at $76.48 a barrel after a ceasefire helped ease supply fears earlier this week. The Aussie dollar held steady at US70.1 cents. The ASX 200 data for today's close wasn't available in the feed, but the local market had a generally soft session based on ETF price action.

politics.summary: Big day for Australian economic policy — the RBA held rates steady, giving mortgage holders a breather. Meanwhile, the Albanese government's CGT (capital gains tax) reform push continues to face political hurdles, and the NDIS is the latest flashpoint in budget negotiations with the Greens.

stories.title: RBA holds interest rates on hold — relief for borrowers
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank decided to leave the official cash rate unchanged today, giving mortgage holders a much-needed break. This is good news for Australian consumers — it means monthly repayments stay the same for now. For investors, steady rates tend to support growth assets like shares and ETFs, which is a mild tailwind for your portfolio.

stories.title: Chalmers winds back ministerial powers in bid to clear CGT Senate hurdle
stories.why_it_matters: Treasurer Chalmers is trying to get his capital gains tax (CGT) reform package through the Senate by giving up some ministerial control over how the rules are applied — a concession designed to win crossbench votes. CGT is the tax you pay when you sell an asset like shares or property for a profit. The proposed changes would affect property investors and anyone selling assets that have appreciated. The reform is still not guaranteed to pass.

stories.title: NDIS reforms face delay as Greens play hardball on budget
stories.why_it_matters: The Greens are refusing to wave through the government's NDIS spending reforms without bigger concessions, creating a logjam in the Senate on the broader budget legislation. The NDIS (National Disability Insurance Scheme) is one of the government's biggest spending programs, and reining in its cost blowout is central to Labor's budget repair plan. A delay here means budget uncertainty drags on, which markets generally don't love.

stories.title: Labor's budget backdown fails to placate the critics
stories.why_it_matters: Despite giving ground on some tax measures, the Albanese government is still copping flak from both the right (who say the CGT changes are anti-investment) and the left (who want more). The political wrangling suggests the government's budget package remains fragile and there could be more changes to come before anything passes the Senate. Worth watching if you hold investment properties or significant share holdings outside super.

ai.summary: Today's AI news is dominated by regulatory debates rather than product launches — governments around the world are arguing about how to govern AI, and there's a cracking deal on AI subscription bundles that's worth knowing about.

stories.title: A Tale of Two AI Policy Regimes — US vs Europe diverging fast
stories.why_it_matters: The US and Europe are taking increasingly different approaches to regulating AI. The US under the current administration is leaning toward light-touch regulation to keep American companies competitive, while the EU is pushing forward with its AI Act — a strict set of rules that classify AI systems by risk level. For investors in US tech like Google and Microsoft, a less regulated US environment is generally good for growth and profit margins.

stories.title: ChatGPT Plus is $240/year — but you can get 5 years of ChatGPT, Claude & Gemini for just $99.99
stories.why_it_matters: A deal circulating online is offering 5 years of access to ChatGPT, Claude (Anthropic's AI) and Gemini (Google's AI) for a one-time $99.99 — compared to ChatGPT Plus alone costing $240 a year. That's genuinely remarkable value if you use any of these tools for work. Practically speaking, this means AI assistants are becoming commodity products, which is a sign of just how fast the market has matured.

stories.title: EU AI Act: Environmental sustainability concerns emerge
stories.why_it_matters: A new angle on the EU's AI Act (Europe's sweeping law governing how AI can be used) is gaining attention — the environmental cost of running large AI systems. Training and running AI models consumes enormous amounts of electricity and water. Regulators are now asking companies to disclose the energy footprint of their AI systems, which could eventually increase operating costs for big AI players like Google and Microsoft.

sport.summary: The Knights scraped past the Dragons in tonight's Round 16 opener, and there's late mail worth knowing ahead of Saturday's games. Also some AFL news that's captured attention nationally.

stories.title: Knights 22 def. Dragons 20 — crucial missed conversion sinks St George
stories.why_it_matters: Newcastle held on for a 22-20 win over St George Illawarra tonight at McDonald Jones Stadium in a real nail-biter. The Dragons had a chance to level it up late but a crucial missed conversion proved the difference. The Knights survive what the ABC called a 'massive scare at home.' Two points the wrong way and this result flips.

stories.title: NRL Late Mail Round 16: Dolphins lose Katoa; Tino rested
stories.why_it_matters: Key late mail ahead of Saturday's games: the Dolphins will be without Edrick Lee Katoa, while Penrith's Isaah Yeo (Tino Fa'asuamaleaui's captain) has been rested ahead of the Titans clash at Cbus Super Stadium on the Gold Coast. The Titans vs Panthers game (5:30pm Saturday) is right in your backyard — worth watching if Penrith are missing key personnel.

stories.title: Should Strange replace Moses for State of Origin Game 3?
stories.why_it_matters: The State of Origin selection debate is heating up ahead of Game 3, with Fox Sports asking whether Mitch Moses should be dropped in favour of another halfback option. Moses has had a mixed series and there's growing pressure on selectors to make a change. Game 3 is the decider if the series is locked at 1-1, so the halfback pick matters enormously.

stories.title: AFL world rallies around icon after devastating health news
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL community has been sending support to a high-profile figure after serious health news broke — exact details are unclear from the available article text, but the response across the football world has been significant. Multiple outlets including News.com.au and Sky News covered the story, suggesting it involves a well-known name. Check the link for the full details.
